intro: Made-to-measure aluminium pergolas, verandas and porches, designed and fitted by the supplier's own team across Ireland, with smaller aluminium work such as bin stores and composite decking.
standfirst: Superior Pergola Ireland builds to measure rather than selling fixed models, so there is no catalogue of sizes. Roofs come in clear glass, tinted glass or polycarbonate, and a pergola can stay open or be closed in with glass sides and sliding doors. The photographs are the supplier's own installations; the selection is PlotNua's.

quoting.title: How a quote works.
quoting.lede: Everything is made to measure, so the published price is where a quote starts, not what you will pay.
steps: Each range has a published from-price that includes fitting. Your price depends on size, roof, sides and extras.
The supplier gives the final price once it has seen and measured the space.
Rough width and depth, whether it fixes to the house wall or stands free, and photos of the spot.
Which roof suits your light and rain; how water drains off it; whether sides or doors can be added later; what the warranty covers for your build; and how long from order to fitting.
quoting.note: From-prices were checked on superiorpergola.ie on 4 November 2026 and can change. The supplier describes its structures as weather-resistant rather than fully waterproof, and its terms make the customer responsible for planning and building-regulation compliance.

considerations: Many open pergolas in a back garden are exempted development, but limits apply. A front porch is exempt only if it is no more than 2 m² in floor area and at least 2 m from a public road, within height limits. A glazed room attached to the house can count as an extension. Check with your local authority before you order.
Glass is clearer and quieter in rain; polycarbonate is lighter and usually cheaper. Tinted glass cuts glare and summer heat but also winter light.
An open pergola is shelter. Adding glass sides and doors makes it a room, which changes how you'll use it, how warm it gets and possibly the planning position.
Ask how the frame fixes to the house or the ground, and where the rainwater goes.
